issues.failure_explanation: The proof gets S_Λ(h)=0 by telescoping over levels. This uses Q_ℓ(1)=1 for every level (so the weights of each univariate rule sum to 1) and the Smolyak combination structure. The fooling function p_n vanishes only at the roots of H_n with n=n_{ℓ̄_1}. It does not vanish at the first-coordinate nodes of lower levels, which are also nodes of the sparse grid. With arbitrarily modified weights on the same node set, those nodes would contribute and S_Λ(h) need not be 0. The result is therefore not weight-independent in the sense claimed. The same overclaim appears in the concluding remarks.

failure_location.quote: consequently, no modification of the weights can improve the rate $N^{-\alpha/2}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to Smolyak/Gauss–Hermite weights with Q_ℓ(1)=1. Alternatively, build a fooling function vanishing at the first-coordinate nodes of all levels ℓ_1≤ℓ̄_1 and prove its univariate lower bound for that node set.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised conclusion that no reweighting of the Gauss–Hermite sparse-grid nodes can beat N^{-α/2} is not established. The theorems themselves remain valid for the actual Smolyak rule.
issues.title: Claim that no modification of the weights can improve the sparse-grid rate is not supported by the proof
issues.why_classification: Weakening the prose is easy, but keeping the advertised weight-independent statement needs a new contained fooling-function argument for a union of node sets.

issues.failure_explanation: The assumption n ≥ e^{d-1} gives only ln n ≥ d-1. It does not give (ln n)^{d-1} ≤ n. For d-1=100 and n=e^{100}, (ln n)^{100}=100^{100}≈10^{200} while n≈2.7·10^{43}. So the stated inequality, and the factor 2 in ln N ≲ 2 ln n, are unjustified. For fixed d, ln N ≲_d ln n does hold, since N ≍_d n(ln n)^{d-1}. But it needs a d-dependent constant, and the hypothesis n ≥ e^{d-1} plays no real role.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false inequality by the d-dependent estimate ln N ≤ ln C_d + ln n + (d-1) ln ln n ≲_d ln n for n ≥ e^{d-1}. This needs only a short rewrite of the step, with the constant allowed to depend on d (as the theorem already permits).
issues.overall_effect: The step relating ln N to ln n_{L-d+1} is unsupported as written. The final bound is still true with a d-dependent constant. The interpolation analogue copies this step.
issues.title: Invalid inference (ln n)^{d-1} ≤ n from n ≥ e^{d-1}
issues.why_classification: A short local estimate fixes the step. The theorem and its rate are unchanged because c_{α,d} is already allowed to depend on d.

issues.failure_explanation: Q_ℓ^{uni} is the n_ℓ-point Gauss–Hermite rule, with nodes the roots of H_{n_ℓ}. The interpolation operator is defined on the zeros of H_{n_ℓ+1}, which are n_ℓ+1 different points. The proof needs ∫ I_{ℓ̄_1}(p_n)ρ = Q_{ℓ̄_1}(p_n), which holds only if interpolation and quadrature share nodes. As defined, I(p_n) need not vanish and the identity fails. The count of evaluation points N also differs from the one used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define I_ℓ^{uni} on the zeros of H_{n_ℓ}, the same n_ℓ nodes as Q_ℓ^{uni}, so that Q_ℓ(g)=∫I_ℓ(g)ρ. Then the existing argument goes through.
issues.overall_effect: The stated lower bounds for sparse-grid interpolation are not proved for the operator as defined. Aligning the nodes with the quadrature fixes this.
issues.title: Interpolation nodes (zeros of H_{n_ℓ+1}) do not match the Gauss–Hermite quadrature nodes used in the proof
issues.why_classification: Changing the node set in the definition makes the existing proof valid with no change to the claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The value $b$ controls the truncation error, namely the integral of $f\rho$ over $\mathbb{R}^d\setminus [-\boldsymbol{b},\boldsymbol{b}]$

issues.failure_explanation: For f≡1 (norm 1) the truncation error is at least P(|x_1|>b)≍e^{-b^2/2}/b. With b^2=(α/2) ln N this is about N^{-α/4}/√(ln N), far larger than N^{-α}(ln N)^{γ}. For general f in H_ρ^α, Cauchy–Schwarz gives truncation error of order e^{-b^2/4}, which needs b^2 ≳ 4α ln N. The digital-net proposition uses b=2√(α ln N) for this reason. The proof of the lattice proposition never treats the truncation error and relies on an external lemma, so the stated b is not shown to suffice. The bound (aff-lattice-error) is false as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose b=c√(α ln N) with c large enough (for example 2, as in prop:added-2) and add the Cauchy–Schwarz estimate of the truncation error by O(N^{-α}). Then re-check that the cited scaled-lattice lemma applies. Only the constants should change, since b stays proportional to √(ln N).
issues.overall_effect: The affinely mapped lattice bound, and the first case of the summary theorem, fail for the stated b. The first case of the summary theorem is the one with exponent 3αd/2+d/4.
issues.title: Truncation parameter b=√((α/2) ln N) cannot give the claimed N^{-α} rate
issues.why_classification: The repair is a parameter change plus a contained truncation estimate and a check of the cited lemma. The structure and rate should survive, but the proof as given does not cover it.
